name: Dynamic Arrays
key_idea: Index, iterate, append and slice arrays and strings; know which operations are O(1) and which are O(n).

name: Hash Set Lookup
key_idea: A set answers 'have I seen this value?' in O(1), replacing an inner search loop.

name: Frequency Counting
key_idea: Map each value to how often it appears; compare or rank values by their counts.

name: Value-to-Index Map
key_idea: Map a value to where you saw it, so a partner or complement can be found in one pass.

name: Canonical Keys
key_idea: Group items by a signature that is equal for equivalent items, such as sorted letters or a count tuple.

name: Bucket Sort by Count
key_idea: When values are bounded by n, use them as array indices to sort or rank in O(n).

name: Prefix and Suffix Accumulation
key_idea: Precompute running totals or products from the left and from the right, then combine them per index.

name: String Encoding
key_idea: Make a reversible encoding by prefixing each piece with its length, so no delimiter can be ambiguous.

name: Sequence Starts
key_idea: Only start counting a run at elements whose predecessor is absent, so each run is walked once.

name: Sort First
key_idea: Sorting costs O(n log n) but unlocks ordered reasoning: pointers, binary search and easy duplicate skipping.

name: Opposite-End Pointers
key_idea: Start at both ends and move the pointer whose move can still improve the answer; each step rules out a set of pairs.

name: Skipping Duplicates
key_idea: In a sorted array, advance past equal neighbours so each distinct combination is produced once.

name: Stack Matching
key_idea: Push openers and pop on closers; the most recent unmatched item is always on top.

name: Running Minimum / Maximum
key_idea: Carry the best value seen so far as you scan, so each position is compared once.

name: Variable Sliding Window
key_idea: Grow the right edge every step; shrink the left edge only while the window breaks the rule.

name: Window with Counts
key_idea: Keep a frequency map of the window and a cheap validity check, updated as items enter and leave.

name: Binary Search
key_idea: Keep an interval where the answer must lie and halve it with each comparison; get the loop bounds exactly right.

name: Search in Rotated Order
key_idea: In a rotated sorted array one half around mid is always sorted; decide which half can hold the target.

name: Linked List Traversal
key_idea: Walk nodes through next pointers; there is no indexing, so track the nodes you need in variables.

name: Reversing Links
key_idea: Reverse with three pointers: prev, current and next, re-pointing one link per step.

name: Dummy Head Node
key_idea: Start a result list at a dummy node so inserting or deleting at the head needs no special case.

name: Fast and Slow Pointers
key_idea: Move one pointer twice as fast: they meet inside a cycle, and the slow one stops at the middle.

name: Fixed-Gap Pointers
key_idea: Advance a lead pointer n steps first; when it reaches the end, the trailing pointer is n from the end.

name: Recursion
key_idea: Solve a problem by trusting the same function on smaller inputs; define the base case first.

name: Tree Depth-First Search
key_idea: Compute a node's answer from its children's answers, or pass information down as arguments.

name: Tree Level-Order Search
key_idea: Process a tree level by level with a queue, taking the current queue length as one level.

name: Binary Search Tree Property
key_idea: Left subtree < node < right subtree everywhere, so in-order is sorted and you can steer by comparison.

name: Building Trees from Traversals
key_idea: Preorder gives the root first; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees.

name: Path Values through a Node
key_idea: Return the best one-sided path to the parent, while updating a global answer with the two-sided path.

name: Tree Serialization
key_idea: Write a traversal that records null children, so the exact shape can be rebuilt.

name: Trie
key_idea: A tree of characters where each path from the root spells a prefix; lookups cost O(word length).

name: Searching with a Trie
key_idea: Walk a trie alongside a DFS so whole branches stop as soon as no word has that prefix.

name: Heap / Priority Queue
key_idea: A heap gives the smallest (or largest) item in O(1) and push or pop in O(log n).

name: Two Heaps
key_idea: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap, balanced in size, to read the median.

name: Backtracking
key_idea: Build a candidate step by step: choose, recurse, then undo the choice before trying the next.

name: Grid Search
key_idea: Treat cells as nodes with up to four neighbours; mark visited cells and check bounds before recursing.

name: Graph Representation
key_idea: Store a graph as an adjacency list built from an edge list.

name: Graph DFS and BFS
key_idea: Visit every reachable node once using a visited set; count components by starting a traversal at each unvisited node.

name: Searching from the Targets
key_idea: Instead of asking where each cell can reach, search backwards from the targets and see which cells they reach.

name: Cycle Detection
key_idea: In a directed graph, a node seen again while still on the current DFS path means a cycle.

name: Topological Sort
key_idea: Repeatedly take nodes with no remaining incoming edges (Kahn's algorithm); leftovers mean a cycle.

name: Union-Find
key_idea: Track connected groups with parent pointers; union merges groups and find returns a group's root.

name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
key_idea: Define dp[i] in words, write its recurrence from smaller indices, and fill it in order (or memoise).

name: Take or Skip
key_idea: At each item choose the better of taking it (with its constraint) or skipping it.

name: Expanding around Centres
key_idea: Every palindrome has a centre; expand from each of the 2n-1 centres while both ends match.

name: Unbounded Choices
key_idea: Build each amount from smaller amounts, allowing every choice to be reused.

name: Prefix Segmentation
key_idea: dp[i] says whether (or how many ways) the first i characters split into valid pieces.

name: Tracking Min and Max
key_idea: When a negative can flip the best into the worst, carry both the max and the min ending here.

name: Subsequence DP
key_idea: dp[i] is the best subsequence ending at i, built from all earlier j that can come before it.

name: 2-D Grid DP
key_idea: A cell's value comes from its top and left neighbours; one row of memory is often enough.

name: DP over Two Strings
key_idea: dp[i][j] answers the question for prefixes a[:i] and b[:j]; match or skip a character from either string.

name: Kadane's Algorithm
key_idea: Extend the current subarray only while its sum helps; otherwise restart at the current element.

name: Greedy Reach
key_idea: Track the farthest index reachable so far; if you ever stand beyond it, you are stuck.

name: Sorting and Merging Intervals
key_idea: Sort by start; an interval overlaps the previous merged one exactly when it starts before that one ends.

name: Greedy by End Time
key_idea: Keep the interval that ends first; it leaves the most room for the rest.

name: Counting Overlaps
key_idea: Process starts in order and release rooms whose end has passed (a min-heap of ends, or sorted starts and ends).

name: Bits and Masks
key_idea: Use &, |, ^, << and >> to read and set bits; n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.

name: XOR Tricks
key_idea: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing everything cancels pairs and leaves the odd one out.

name: DP on Bits
key_idea: Reuse answers for smaller numbers: bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).

name: Arithmetic with Bits
key_idea: Addition is XOR for the sum without carry, plus AND shifted left for the carry, repeated until no carry is left.

name: Matrix Index Tricks
key_idea: Express moves as index transformations: transpose, reverse rows, or walk layers with four boundaries.

name: In-Place Markers
key_idea: Reuse part of the input (a first row or column, or a sign) as flags to avoid extra memory.
